title: Soft-commit Capacity Pocket — one-to-one prep + micro-scenarios
content:
Purpose / context:
- Pocket notes for my one-to-one with Jack. Goal: align on soft-commit strategy for Dedicated GPU pools, surface risks, and leave with a 3-point action list.
- Audience: me (ops lead), Jack (capacity owner), Elena (policy/quotas).

Top-line summary to say in the 1:1:
- We have short-term demand growth in text-gen workloads + a spike in inference tests from Partner X. Recommend a small soft-commit increase (10–12% of pool) with conditional autoscale burst.
- Need agreement on headroom policy (min buffer for p95 latency), plus a guardrail for cost during burst windows.

Quick state (back-of-envelope, rough numbers):
- Current dedicated pool: 48 x A100-80GB (baseline config).
- Baseline utilization last 7d (avg): 62% overall, peak days hit 84% for short periods (1–2 hours).
- Typical token throughput: ~3.2B tokens/day across pool during peak weekdays.
- Current reserved (hard) commitments: 40 units (equiv. to ~40 GPUs for a different contract shape).

Micro-scenarios I want to walk through (3):
1) Conservative bump (soft-commit +10%, no burst):
   - Provisioning: +5 GPUs logical soft-commit overlay (soft routing, no billing change until used).
   - Autoscale: disabled for this bump.
   - Expected effect: reduced p95 latency incidents by ~30–40% during mid peaks.
   - Risk: insufficient for large partner test spikes.

2) Soft-commit + burst window (preferred):
   - Provisioning: +10% soft-commit (≈ +5 GPUs) + policy to allow burst up to +15% during reserved windows (2 hours, clearly tagged).
   - Billing guardrail: cap burst spend to $X/hour (flip to cheaper model variant if exceeded).
   - Expectation: covers Partner X integration tests and weekend load test.
   - Risk: bursts may cause overprovision if tests run long — need auto-fallback to model-quantized variant.

3) Aggressive reserve (sales-driven, runway commit):
   - Move to hard-reserve +15 GPUs for 3 months (requires negotiation with sales/legal).
   - Benefits: predictable latency, lower per-token cost.
   - Drawbacks: contract inertia if traffic drops.

Open questions to ask Jack in the 1:1:
- How confident is infra in preemption/fallback if burst overshoot happens? (SRE input)
- Can we attach a token-level QoS tag so Partner X tests get priority KV-cache hot paths?
- Is there a simple toggle to restrict burst to only specific model families to limit cost?

Quick ops checklist (what I want decided by end of meeting):
- Decide which micro-scenario to try next billing cycle (Conservative / Burst / Aggressive).
- Agree on a cost cap for burst windows and owner to monitor it.
- Identify fallback model variant and owner to implement fallback hook (deadline: next patch).

Back-of-envelope cost calc for burst scenario (very rough):
- A100-80GB spot-ish baseline: $X/GPU-hour (accounting mix of reserved/spot).
- +10% on 48 GPUs => +4.8 ≈ 5 GPUs.
- If burst for 2 hours/day on avg weekdays (10 days/month): 5 GPUs * 2 hrs * 10 days = 100 GPU-hours/month.
- 100 GPU-hours/month * $X => put a placeholder $X so we can swap in exact rate during meeting.

Short script / language to use in calendar invite or Slack follow-up:
- "Quick one-to-one to finalize soft-commit approach for Dedicated pools; want to pick between a modest soft bump, a burst-window policy, or pursuing a short-term hard reserve. I'll bring cost guardrail options and fallback plan. Expect 20 minutes."

Notes to self (bullet-style, stream-of-consciousness):
- If Jack prefers hard reserve, loop in Sales to re-check discount tiers (DCP-117 probably relevant).
- Ask Elena to draft a burst policy template (what counts as a burst, alert thresholds, cost cap).
- Consider a canary: enable burst for non-production tag first for 24h and measure tail latency.
- Add telemetry: token-level cost per model per route for the burst window (we already have traces but need aggregated dashboard).

Follow-ups (owners & tentative deadlines):
- Jack: confirm risk tolerance and preferred micro-scenario (due: 2025-02-20).
- Elena: draft burst policy + alert thresholds (due: 2025-02-22).
- Maya (me): prepare a short dashboard showing p50/p95 token latency vs utilization for last 30 days (due: 2025-02-19).
- SRE (cc Jack): confirm fallback automation feasibility (ticket: INF-3421) and ETA (due: 2025-02-24).

One-liners to say if conversation goes long:
- "Start small: soft bump + monitored burst gives us breathing room without contract lock-in."
- "If partner tests prove persistent, we can escalate to a reserve and amortize cost with sales."

Random scribbles / hypotheses to test while preparing dashboard:
- Hypothesis A: p95 correlates strongly with small spikes in short-lived micro-bursts (less than 5s). If true, a small soft-commit will drastically reduce incidents.
- Hypothesis B: KV-cache cold misses during partner tests are driving 60% of latency variance. If true, we should prioritize cache warmers for partner routes.

Slack snippet to post after the 1:1 (if agreed on burst):
- "We agreed to pilot a +10% soft-commit with up to +15% burst windows for partner tests. Cost cap set at $[placeholder]/hr. Elena to publish formal policy. Jack to monitor. Will revert with dashboard in 48h."

End of pocket notes. Keep this lightweight — bring numbers and one recommendation.
